title: bug: ProtectedStateStore treats a non-directory root as an absent record
description: Windows repro in CQ-RF02 D4: replace ProtectedStateStore.root with a regular file, then read a hash-named record; the child lookup throws NoSuchFileException and read returns null before validating the root. After an IDE restart profile() therefore returns LEGACY instead of fail-closed PROTECTED. Validate an existing/unreadable/non-directory root before treating a record as confirmed absent; preserve genuinely absent fresh stores. Evidence: /tmp/rf02-green.log, RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest line 210.
definitionOfDone: A root that exists as a regular file never yields a confirmed-absent read; callers fail closed, with Windows regression coverage.
A genuinely absent root/record still reads null; owner-only, link/junction, size and atomic-write behavior remain unchanged.
Fresh Windows JetBrains Gradle tests pass under jetbrains-gradle lease.

PS6 has NO assume, so it is DoD 1's unconditional Windows regression:
(a) `newStore().read(NAME_A)` is null: a fresh root below a directory.
(b) Make the root a regular file: `Files.createDirectories(root.parent)`, then `Files.writeString(root, "not a directory")`. `read(NAME_A)` throws `ProtectedStateStore.Untrusted` on every OS, and the file still holds "not a directory".
(c) Make the root's parent `moe` a regular file: on a fresh newStore(), `Files.writeString(root.parent, "not a directory")`. `read(NAME_A)` throws, never returns null. Assert `IOException::class.java` and say why in a comment: Windows throws Untrusted, POSIX throws the lookup's own 'Not a directory' FileSystemException.

PS7 holds the assume-gated rows, so a host without links or ACLs skips only these:
(d) Write NAME_B to a store, then `loosen(root, directory = true)`. `read(NAME_A)`, an absent record, throws Untrusted.
(e) Make a root that links to another store's owner-only root, with `symlink(linkedRoot.root, elsewhere.root)`. `read(NAME_A)`, absent, throws Untrusted.
(f) Make a linked PARENT: `symlink(tmp/linked-system, newFolder())`. Then `ProtectedStateStore(system.resolve("moe/protected-state")).read(NAME_A)` is null, and a write of NAME_A reads back. This guards that only the root, never its parents, must be link-free, since a real IDE system directory may sit behind a link.

implementationPlan.description:
FIX ProtectedStateStore.read. Change only read() and add two private helpers. RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt is NOT edited, because its callers already fail closed on any throw:
- storedProfile catches Exception and returns UNTRUSTED, which gives PROTECTED plus one downgrade ask;
- load() catches Exception and returns null, so the unverified daemon is refused.

1. read(name): keep `val file = fileFor(name)` first, so the name check is unchanged. Then:
   `if (!present(root)) { requireDirectoryAbove(root); return null }`
   `requireOwnerOnly(root, directory = true)`
   `if (!present(file)) return null`
   `requireOwnerOnly(file, directory = false)`
   The NOFOLLOW_LINKS stream read and the MAX_BYTES cap follow, unchanged. The root is now validated BEFORE any record lookup. A present record still gets the same two checks in the same order.
2. `private fun present(path: Path): Boolean`: `Files.readAttributes(path, BasicFileAttributes::class.java, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)` gives true, and NoSuchFileException gives false.
3. `private fun requireDirectoryAbove(path: Path)`:
   - find the nearest present ancestor with `generateSequence(path.parent) { it.parent }.firstOrNull(::present)`, and return when there is none;
   - throw `Untrusted("the protected state root is not under a directory")` unless `Files.isDirectory(it)` holds;
   - call isDirectory WITHOUT NOFOLLOW_LINKS: a linked IDE system directory is legitimate, and only the root itself must be a real directory.
4. Comments, in the file's style:
   - read's KDoc says it returns null only when nothing can be stored there yet: no root below a directory, or no file in an owner-only root.
   - One comment gives the why: Windows answers a lookup through a regular file as missing, so an unchecked root let a broken store read as empty.

Error handling: present() swallows ONLY NoSuchFileException. Every other IOException propagates out of read(): an AccessDeniedException from an unreadable root, a POSIX ENOTDIR FileSystemException, or an ACL read failure. Callers keep catching Exception and fail closed. No new catch-all, and no logging of paths or contents (Untrusted messages name the broken rule only).

About DoD 2's 'unchanged': every case that is refused today stays refused, and every present-record read accepted today stays accepted. The one intended change is that an existing invalid root (a file, a link, or a loosened or unreadable directory) no longer confirms absence. That is the task's 'validate an existing root before treating a record as confirmed absent'.

Leave write, delete, restrict, isOwnerOnly, requireKind, usableFor, forIde, NAME and MAX_BYTES byte-identical.

All other store members untouched. Expected-red evidence is preserved in /tmp/bf4debb3-red.log and /tmp/bf4debb3-red.xml. executionContract.intendedBehavior: ProtectedStateStore.read(name) returns null only for a confirmed-absent record. Confirmed absent means either the root is missing and its nearest existing parent is a directory (links followed), or the root is an owner-only, link-free directory without that file. Every other existing root throws before any record lookup, on Windows as on POSIX: a regular file, a link or junction, or a loosened, deny-ACL or unreadable directory. A missing root below a regular file also throws. RuntimeSelectionPolicy then fails closed: profile() gives PROTECTED plus one downgrade ask, and the provenance check refuses. A present record reads exactly as before.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) Catch the child's NoSuchFileException, then check only that the root is a regular file. Rejected: a linked or loosened root, and on Windows a regular-file parent, would still confirm absence.
(2) Have RuntimeSelectionPolicy treat ABSENT under a broken store as UNTRUSTED. Rejected: only the store knows whether its root is valid. That would be a second owner-only check, and RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt is RF02's file (mem:gotcha-protected-state-absent-root says not to).
(3) Put the tests in a new ProtectedStateStoreTest.kt. Rejected: it would duplicate the newStore, symlink/junction and loosen helpers. PS1-PS5 already live in RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest, and that file is serialized: RF02 is blocked on this task, and RF04 and task-0c72d59a depend on RF02.
(4) Use the full `test --rerun` gate. Rejected: MoeDaemonSupervisorTest:175 is task-f23c4464's known red, and the two fixes would deadlock waiting on each other. RF02 and task-90664db1 own the full gate once both land.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: A lookup through a regular file throws NoSuchFileException on Windows (ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND) but FileSystemException 'Not a directory' (ENOTDIR) on POSIX. So Linux already failed closed for a file root, and Windows read it as absent; that is RF02's repro in /tmp/rf02-green.log, D4 line 210. Under NOFOLLOW_LINKS, Java reports a Windows junction as isDirectory && isOther, and requireKind already refuses that. Files.isDirectory with no options follows links. Files.createDirectories uses the same nearest-existing-parent walk. The only callers of read() are in RuntimeSelectionPolicy, storedProfile and load(), and both catch Exception. HEAD 52d45cb6 holds RF02's checkpoint 91eb0d14 and task-90664db1's checkpoint; the moe-jetbrains tree was clean at planning time. CI runs ./gradlew test on ubuntu-latest, so every assertion must hold on POSIX too, which is why (c) asserts IOException.
planningNotes.risks:
- Checking parents WITH NOFOLLOW_LINKS would make every fresh store under a symlinked or junctioned IDE system directory UNTRUSTED. Every legacy project would then get a downgrade dialog. PS7 (f) guards this.
- For an absent record, the root's ACL is now read on every profile() call. That is the same cost a present record already pays, and it is not a hot loop.
- RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest.kt is in RF02's filesModified, which makes it contested for wrapper landing; see step 4.
- A peer's in-progress .kt can break the shared-tree compile (see the peer-red gotcha).
- The gradlew client can run out of memory without GRADLE_OPTS.
- Never edit RF02's D1-D5 rows or MoeDaemonSupervisorTest.kt.
- Two BLOCKED tasks (RF02 and task-90664db1) auto-unblock only once this task and task-f23c4464 are both DONE, so keep the scope tight.
